page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. This instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression performing in the bottom 10%. However, the instance leverages its 24 vCPUs to deliver average multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks reside in the average tier, with uncached read and write speeds reaching 96.89 GB/sec and 52.55 GB/sec respectively.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not demand top-tier single-thread compute speeds. The high RAM allocation relative to vCPUs makes it well-suited for hosting relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise middleware. It is also capable of handling multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and moderate LLM inference text generation using medium-sized models, where its average multi-core throughput can be fully utilized.
